subject: Re: Redwood Inference - Procurement & Payment Path (PO vs Card)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@finopsco.com>, Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@finopsco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Procurement & payment path (PO vs card) — next steps

Hi Sophie / Oliver —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can get procurement moving: 

Recap (from today's discovery):
- FinOpsCo prefers vendor onboarding via their AP portal and typically requires a PO + invoice for mid-market deals (> $50k ARR).
- For pilots or POCs under ~$15k, they sometimes approve a corporate card payment to accelerate time-to-value, but AP needs a formal vendor profile first.
- FinOpsCo is evaluating AWS Marketplace as an easier procurement path — you indicated Marketplace listing would simplify procurement but would require product packaging and a short legal review.

Options I recommend (pick one and we can action):
1) Standard procurement (preferred by AP): We provide the vendor onboarding docs + SOW; you issue a PO (Net30) and we invoice. I can send a templated SOW and vendor checklist that aligns with your AP requirements.
2) Pilot on card (fastest): We can accept a corporate card for a 90-day pilot (one-time charge). We still need vendor onboarding metadata (W-9, bank details optional) to register in your system.
3) Marketplace: If you want to go via AWS Marketplace, we can initiate packaging — longer lead time but lowers internal procurement friction for renewals.

Attachments: Redwood-Vendor-Onboarding-Checklist.pdf, Redwood-SOW-Template-90d-trial.pdf, SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2026.pdf (SOC2 attestation for vendor review).

Next steps I propose:
- Sophie / Oliver: confirm preferred path (PO vs card vs marketplace)
- If PO: please share AP contact and PO template / required fields so we can pre-fill SOW and vendor form
- If card: confirm billing contact and any internal card spend approval process
- If Marketplace: confirm owner for Marketplace packaging and legal reviewer

I can set up a 30-min procurement sync for Monday to walk through vendor onboarding if that's helpful.

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0123

From: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@finopsco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@finopsco.com>, AP Team <ap@finopsco.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Procurement & payment path (PO vs card) — next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from AP side:
- FinOpsCo's default for new vendors is vendor onboarding + PO (Net30). For transactions expected > $25k we require PO and 2-step approvals.
- For a short pilot (<= $10k), Procurement can approve a card payment on the vendor's profile once the vendor form (W-9 + vendor contact + remit address) is in our system.
- AWS Marketplace would be ideal long-term but Procurement will still want a vendor relationship established before procurement teams agree to marketplace purchasing for this product category.

Can you send the vendor profile fields we need to enter? Also, is Redwood willing to accept a single one-time card payment for the 90-day trial, and then convert to PO/Net30 if we decide to expand?

Oliver, looping you to confirm AP contact for issuing a PO (and any vendor portal links).

Thanks,
Sophie
Director, Procurement | FinOpsCo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@finopsco.com>, Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@finopsco.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T14:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Procurement & payment path (PO vs card) — next steps

Hi Sophie / Oliver —

Yes — we can support both flows. Details below and what we'll provide immediately: 

1) Vendor onboarding / PO (recommended for BAU)
- What we need from FinOpsCo: PO with line items (or a PO number + billing contact) and any vendor portal link or form fields.
- What we will provide: Completed vendor onboarding packet (attached), pre-filled SOW template for a 90-day pilot with pricing and acceptance criteria, Redwood's W-9 and SOC2 (attached), and our standard invoice template.

2) Card (accelerated pilot)
- We can accept a one-time corporate card payment for a 90-day pilot up to $10k.
- If you want to do an initial card payment and then convert to PO for expansion, that's fine — we'll credit the initial payment against the first invoice under the PO. We'll document that in the SOW so AP sees the crediting.

3) Marketplace
- We can start an AWS Marketplace packaging conversation in parallel. Marketplace listing reduces friction for future purchases, but packaging + listing will add 2-4 weeks for legal/compliance work.

Next actions from Redwood (me):
- Attach vendor packet (attached) and pre-fill SOW once you share the PO template/required fields.
- Send a DocuSign SOW if PO path chosen; otherwise, provide payment link for card pilot.

Proposed immediate next step: 15-min procurement-form walk-through on Tue 2/16 to confirm portal fields and required documents. Are you available?

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood-Vendor-Onboarding-Checklist.pdf, Redwood-SOW-Template-90d-trial.pdf, SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2026.pdf

From: Oliver Hayes <oliver.hayes@finopsco.com>

Marissa / Sophie —

We can do the PO route. I'll have AP issue a PO (Net30) once you return the pre-filled SOW and vendor packet — please include the remit address and Redwood's tax ID on the vendor form.

Marissa, please send pre-filled docs to ap@finopsco.com and cc me.

Sophie — happy to join the Tue 2/16 15-min walk-through; will add to the calendar.

Thanks,
Oliver
Head of Finance Operations | FinOpsCo
